"Every winter my mother took out the album and laughed at the girl in the striped bathing suit. 'Look at us! Who dressed us like that?' she would say. Now she is gone, and I take out the same album. I do not laugh. It is her laughter I remember when I turn the pages, and that is the picture I cannot hold in my hand."

Answer the following:
(i) What did the mother do every winter?  (a) She burnt old photos  (b) She went to the beach  (c) She painted pictures  (d) She looked at the album and laughed
(ii) How is the narrator's reaction different from her mother's?
(iii) Which line of thought in "A Photograph" is reflected here?
(iv) "The picture I cannot hold in my hand" refers to …  (a) the memory of her mother's laughter  (b) a lost photo  (c) a broken frame  (d) a painting
items.answer: (i) (d) She looked at the album and laughed (ii) The mother laughed fondly; the narrator does not laugh but grieves. (iii) The mother's past was the holiday; the daughter's past is the mother's laughter. (iv) (a) the memory of her mother's laughter
items.markingKey: (i) (d) She looked at the album and laughed (ii) The mother laughed fondly; the narrator does not laugh but grieves. (iii) The mother's past was the holiday; the daughter's past is the mother's laughter. (iv) (a) the memory of her mother's laughter (1 mark each, 4 marks.)

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the theme of loss in 'A Photograph' is correct?
items.answer: The photograph is a link between the poet and her dead mother.
items.markingKey: (c) Correct: "The photograph is a link between the poet and her dead mother." The other statements contradict the text.
options: The poet is happy that her mother is gone.
The poem says the sea has changed more than the people.
The photograph is a link between the poet and her dead mother.
The poem celebrates the permanence of human life.

items.stem: You are Aryan. Write an article in 120–150 words on "Photographs: Windows to Our Past".
items.answer: An article covering: title and byline; value of photographs; family memories; digital vs printed photos; conclusion.
items.markingKey: Format (1): a catchy title and the writer's name (byline). Content: introduction, body paragraphs with causes, effects or examples, and a conclusion with suggestions or a call to action. Content (2 marks): title and byline; value of photographs; family memories; digital vs printed photos; conclusion. Expression (2 marks): fluency, accuracy of grammar and spelling, appropriate register and word limit.
